DAS-S2-A1.title: Sorting the rows of a matrix
DAS-S2-A1.description: Sort every row of an n × m matrix in ascending order.
DAS-S2-A1.instructions: Input: n m; then n lines of m integers. Output: the sorted matrix, one row per line, separated by single spaces.

DAS-S2-A2.title: Binary search
DAS-S2-A2.description: In an array sorted in ascending order without repeats, find the position of every query with binary search.
DAS-S2-A2.instructions: Input: n; n numbers; q; then q queries x. Output: for every query, on its own line, the index (from 1) or -1.
DAS-S2-A2.constraintsText: 1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5, 1 ≤ q ≤ 10^5. Linear search exceeds the time limit.

DAS-S2-A3.title: GCD and LCM functions
DAS-S2-A3.description: Write two functions: gcd(a, b) with Euclid's algorithm and lcm(a, b) = a / gcd(a, b) · b. The main program uses them.
DAS-S2-A3.instructions: Input: a b. Output: the GCD and the LCM on one line.
DAS-S2-A3.constraintsText: 1 ≤ a, b ≤ 10^9 (the LCM fits in a long).

DAS-S2-A4.title: Fast exponentiation by recursion
DAS-S2-A4.description: Compute aⁿ mod m with a recursive function: if n is even, aⁿ = (a^(n/2))², if odd, aⁿ = a · aⁿ⁻¹. This takes O(log n) steps.
DAS-S2-A4.instructions: Input: a n m. Output: aⁿ mod m.

DAS-S2-A5.title: Elements above the average (a dynamic array)
DAS-S2-A5.description: Create an array whose size is known only at run time (a Python list, new long[n] or an ArrayList in Java) and print the elements greater than the arithmetic mean in input order.
DAS-S2-A5.instructions: Input: n; n integers. Output: the elements strictly greater than the mean, separated by spaces; if there are none, -.
DAS-S2-A5.constraintsText: 1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5. To avoid fractions, check the condition aᵢ · n > sum.

DAS-S2-A6.title: ASCII codes of characters
DAS-S2-A6.description: Print the ASCII code of every character of a line (a space is a character too: 32).
DAS-S2-A6.instructions: Input: one line (ASCII characters only). Output: the codes separated by spaces.
DAS-S2-A6.constraintsText: The line is 1 to 200 characters long.

DAS-S2-A7.title: A palindrome string
DAS-S2-A7.description: Decide whether a line is a palindrome: only letters and digits count, and case is ignored.
DAS-S2-A7.instructions: Input: one line (ASCII). Output: Palindrom or Palindrom emas ("not a palindrome"; the answers are in Uzbek — that is how the tests check them).
DAS-S2-A7.constraintsText: The line is 1 to 1000 characters long.

DAS-S2-A8.title: Text statistics (working with a stream)
DAS-S2-A8.description: Read standard input to its end, like a file, and count the lines, words and characters (line-end characters are not counted).
DAS-S2-A8.instructions: Input: one or more lines of text. Output: three numbers on one line — lines, words, characters.
DAS-S2-A8.constraintsText: The text is up to 100 KB.

DAS-S2-MT1.title: The maximum of an array and its position (a function parameter)
DAS-S2-MT1.description: Write a function that takes an array as a parameter and returns the largest element and its first position.
DAS-S2-MT1.instructions: Input: n; n numbers. Output: the maximum and its position (from 1).

DAS-S2-MT2.title: Multiplying matrices
DAS-S2-MT2.description: Write a function that takes matrices A (n × m) and B (m × p) and returns C = A · B.
DAS-S2-MT2.instructions: Input: n m p; the n rows of A; the m rows of B. Output: the n rows of C.

DAS-S2-MT3.title: Merging two sorted arrays
DAS-S2-MT3.description: Merge two arrays sorted in ascending order into one sorted array. Do not use a ready sort function: the two-pointer method runs in O(n + m).
DAS-S2-MT3.instructions: Input: n; the array a; m; the array b. Output: the merged array.

DAS-S2-MT4.title: The Towers of Hanoi (recursion)
DAS-S2-MT4.description: Move n disks from peg 1 to peg 3: one disk at a time, and a larger disk never goes on a smaller one. Recursion: n−1 disks to the spare peg, the largest to the target, then the n−1 disks on top of it.
DAS-S2-MT4.instructions: Input: n. Output: the number of moves on the first line, then every move on its own line: from where to where.

DAS-S2-MT5.title: The Ackermann function (nested recursion)
DAS-S2-MT5.description: A(0, n) = n + 1; A(m, 0) = A(m − 1, 1); A(m, n) = A(m − 1, A(m, n − 1)). A call inside a call — the classic example of nested recursion.
DAS-S2-MT5.instructions: Input: m n. Output: A(m, n).
DAS-S2-MT5.constraintsText: 0 ≤ m ≤ 3, 0 ≤ n ≤ 5. In Python set sys.setrecursionlimit(10000).

DAS-S2-MT6.title: Capitalising words
DAS-S2-MT6.description: Start every word of a line with a capital letter and make the remaining letters lowercase. Leave a single space between words.
DAS-S2-MT6.instructions: Input: one line (ASCII letters and spaces). Output: the formatted line.
DAS-S2-MT6.constraintsText: The line is 1 to 1000 characters long, with at least one word.

DAS-S2-MT7.title: A bank account class
DAS-S2-MT7.description: Create a BankAccount class: the balance field is private and is managed through the deposit, withdraw and balance methods. A withdrawal is refused if there are not enough funds.
DAS-S2-MT7.instructions: Input: n; then n commands: deposit X, withdraw X or balance. Output: the current balance for every balance command; for a refused withdrawal, Mablag yetarli emas ("insufficient funds"; the message is in Uzbek — that is how the tests check it).
DAS-S2-MT7.constraintsText: 1 ≤ n ≤ 1000, 1 ≤ X ≤ 10^9. The starting balance is 0.
